findings.reason: Standalone original-resolution image has no figure. A concrete crossing plot materially clarifies how two smooth fixed-coordinate eigenvalue lines have an ordered maximum whose eigenspace switches between orthogonal coordinate lines. The double eigenspace must be identified at the crossing. This meets the authorized explanatory-diagram criterion; the existing proof is retained.
findings.action: Added a fenced TikZ crossing plot and its explanatory paragraph in final Remarks.

correction: Added final Remarks illustrating eigenvalues t and -t, ordered maximum |t|, side-dependent top eigenspaces, and the full double eigenspace at zero. No original claim or proof text changed.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Real symmetric matrix A(t)=diag(t,-t), parameter t in R, coordinate vectors e1,e2.
diagram_math_checks.check: Direct multiplication gives A(t)e1=t e1 and A(t)e2=-t e2, matching the two straight lines and the original displayed family and Counterexample step 1.1.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Top eigenvalue and eigenspace on either side
diagram_math_checks.check: For t<0, -t>t, so the thick upper-left half is -t with span{e2}; for t>0, t>-t, so the thick upper-right half is t with span{e1}. The thick polyline is exactly lambda=|t| and both original side labels agree with step 1.1.

t=-t only at t=0. A(0) is the zero 2x2 matrix, whose sole eigenvalue zero has algebraic multiplicity two and eigenspace E0=R^2. The dot records a double eigenvalue, never a selected unique eigendirection.

The graph depicts eigenvalues and labels eigenspaces, not an eigenvector interpolation. The fixed-coordinate eigenvalue lines have slopes +1 and -1; the ordered maximum |t| has one-sided slopes -1,+1. The original no-continuous-nonzero-eigenvector obstruction in step 2.1 remains a separate argument based on the distinct limiting eigendirections; no derivative of an eigenvector is inferred from the graph.
The original two-step proof, its Given, supplier reference and justification tags remain byte-identical; the figure is outside all proof-like sections in Remarks.
